search_log: Searched “Patriot Games Tom Clancy excerpt first chapter,” “point of view third person narrator,” “Google Books preview,” and “Internet Archive text.”
Opened and reviewed the Penguin Random House authorized Chapter 1 excerpt, the Tom Clancy website PDF excerpt, Google Books metadata/preview page, and BookRags point-of-view analysis.

Searched specifically for “Patriot Games” with “first person,” “alternating point of view,” and “omniscient narrator”; results corroborated third-person omniscience and produced no credible evidence of sustained first-person, second-person, or alternating base sections.
Google Books and Open Library supplied bibliographic or limited-preview material but no additional accessible structural evidence, so they were not used as person-supporting sources.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third-person, moving among character viewpoints. Multiple interior Goodreads passages expose external narration of Sally, Ryan, and others, while dialogue, maxims, the Burke epigraph, and Clancy-attributed paratext were excluded from base-person inference. The authorized opening independently shows sustained third-person narration; its momentary “I” is free-direct thought belonging to Ryan, not a narrator switch. The whole-book point-of-view description corroborates third-person omniscience, and targeted research found no alternating structure. The main limitation is that the Tier A prose covers only the opening, mitigated by the interior quote evidence and explicit whole-book description.
